title: Hippocampal sclerosis: A review on current research status and its mechanisms.
authors: Zhao, Ting; Cui, Xiaoxiao; Zhang, Xinru; Zhao, Mengke; Rastegar-Kashkooli, Yousef; Wang, Junyang; Li, Qiang; Jiang, Chao; Li, Nan; Xing, Fei; Han, Xiong; Zhang, Jiewen; Xing, Na; Wang, Junmin; Wang, Jian
one_liner_zh: 综述海马硬化病理机制与影像诊断，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Hippocampal sclerosis (HS) is a pathological condition characterized by significant loss of hippocampal neurons and gliosis. This condition represents the most common neuropathological change observed in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) and is also found in aging individuals. TLE related to HS is the most prevalent type of drug-resistant epilepsy in adults, and its underlying mechanisms are not yet fully understood. Therefore, developing improved methods for predicting and treating drug-resistant patients with TLE-HS is crucial. Patients with TLE-HS often experience cognitive impairment and psychological comorbidities, significantly affecting their quality of life. Consequently, a thorough review of the current research status of TLE-HS is essential, focusing on its prediction, diagnosis, treatment, and underlying mechanisms. The hippocampus plays a pivotal role in memory and cognition. HS of aging (HS-Aging), a condition linked to dementia in the ultra-elderly, is marked by severe CA1 (cornu ammonis) neuronal loss and frequent transactive response DNA-binding protein of 43 kDa (TDP-43) proteinopathy, often misdiagnosed as Alzheimer's disease (AD). Nonetheless, clinical characteristics and patterns of hippocampal atrophy can help differentiate between the two disorders. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the pathological features of HS, the relevant mechanisms underlying TLE-HS and HS-Aging, current imaging diagnostic techniques, including machine learning, and available treatment modalities. It also explores the prognosis and comorbidities related to these conditions. Future research directions include establishing animal models to clarify the poorly understood mechanisms underlying HS, particularly those related to emotional processing. Investigating post-HS behavioral and cognitive changes in these models will lay the foundation for further advancements in this field. This review is a cornerstone for future investigations and suggests additional research endeavors.
abstract_zh: 海马硬化（Hippocampal sclerosis, HS）是一种以海马神经元显著丢失和胶质增生为特征的病理状态。该状况是颞叶癫痫（temporal lobe epilepsy, TLE）患者中最常见的神经病理改变，也见于老年个体中。与HS相关的TLE是成人中最常见的耐药性癫痫类型，其潜在机制尚未完全明了。因此，开发改进的方法来预测和治疗TLE-HS耐药患者至关重要。TLE-HS患者常伴有认知障碍和心理合并症，严重影响其生活质量。鉴于此，对TLE-HS的预测、诊断、治疗及其潜在机制进行全面的研究现状综述显得尤为必要。海马在记忆和认知中扮演关键角色。老年性海马硬化（HS-Aging），一种与超高龄老人痴呆相关的状况，其特征是CA1（cornu ammonis）区神经元严重丢失及频繁出现43 kDa反式激活反应DNA结合蛋白（TDP-43）蛋白病，常被误诊为阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）。尽管如此，临床特征和海马萎缩模式有助于区分这两种疾病。本综述旨在全面概述HS的病理特征、TLE-HS和HS-Aging的相关机制、当前影像诊断技术（包括机器学习）及可用治疗方式，并探讨这些状况的预后及合并症。未来研究方向包括建立动物模型以阐明HS中理解不足的机制，特别是与情绪处理相关的机制。在这些模型中研究HS后的行为和认知变化，将为该领域的进一步发展奠定基础。本综述是未来研究的基础，并提出了进一步的研究方向。
